summary.intent: Continue optimizing the callisto `release` command after PR #364, by batching per-package git work in a way consistent with the project's architecture and semantic models.
summary.outcome: Rewrote the version-commit check in `version_commit.rs` to use the existing batched GitAccess primitives (stacked on #364's `in_parallel`). Fixed test runners that lacked stdin support, got full CI green, and committed, pushed and opened a stacked PR.

repo: GitAccess already provides batched primitives (`object_ids` and the `git_batch` module, including `batch_blobs`/`BatchBlob`), so batching git work should use these rather than new ad hoc process spawning.
changed.rs compares directories by tree id, a pattern reusable for the version-commit check.
The `in_parallel` helper was introduced in PR #364, so follow-up perf work must be built on that branch, which is why a native PR stack is used.
The production git runner supports piping stdin, but several test CommandRunner implementations that wrap real git did not; batched `cat-file --batch` style calls expose that gap.
Test runners wrapping real git that needed stdin delegation: the test `RealGitRunner`, `StubbedRemote` (release/mod.rs:139), and `OfflineRunner` in release/local.rs.
Remaining cost: `cargo info` is about 100 ms per crate; it was kept because it honors the user's cargo config and credentials.
Guard tests for the version-commit check (nine, including inherited-version and merged-branch cases) effectively catch behavior regressions in the rewrite.

code.finding: `StubbedRemote` wraps real git for local.rs tests and had to be changed to delegate stdin-capable execution to the underlying runner.
`OfflineRunner` also lacked stdin support and needed the same delegation fix for batched git calls to pass CI.

workflow: Read the architecture docs and existing helpers before rewriting, so new code stays inside project conventions.
When a change depends on an unmerged PR, merge that branch in and open the new PR as the next one in a native stack.
Run the guard unit tests first, then full CI, and fix each failure by finding all similar cases (e.g. grep for all test CommandRunner impls) rather than one at a time.
Measure before and after (timing and process counts) at several workspace sizes (N=10, N=30).

friction: The batched implementation was first swapped in on a branch without `in_parallel`, so it had to be restored and #364 merged in.
Full CI failed in several rounds, each exposing another test runner without stdin support (RealGitRunner, StubbedRemote, OfflineRunner).
Scratch files were written to /tmp via helper scripts and a Python swap script rather than direct edits.
open_items: Reading the crates.io sparse index directly for public crates would cut lookup from about 100 ms to about 40 ms per crate and parallelize fully; it is a design change awaiting the user's decision.
Dogfooding other ecosystems for further findings is planned but not yet done.
The stacked batching PR depends on #364 and the release PR #349 remains open.
